title: Madhuri Dixit Has a Dead Body in Her Kitchen. Also, the No. 1 Spot on Netflix India.
excerpt: Maa Behen is a sharp, chaotic dark comedy about a mother and two daughters covering up a crime — and Triptii Dimri steals every frame she's in.
body:
Here's the setup: a dead body turns up in Rekha's kitchen. Rekha is a single mother in a small Indian town. She is also played by Madhuri Dixit, which means she handles the situation with the kind of composed panic that only a woman who's been navigating male incompetence for decades can muster. She calls her two daughters. They come. They argue. They try to make the body disappear before the neighbours find out.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=xYbLpsEhcfA

That's Maa Behen, and it's currently the No. 1 title on Netflix India.

Directed by Suresh Triveni — who proved with Jalsa that he knows how to make women's stories uncomfortable and compelling in equal measure — the film is a dark comedy that moves at the pace of a panic attack. Over the course of a single chaotic night, Rekha and her daughters Jaya (Triptii Dimri) and Sushma (Dharna Durgaa) try to keep their secret from a neighbourhood that runs on gossip, moral policing, and the assumption that any woman living independently must be up to something.

https://x.com/NetflixIndia/status/2063221870225137805

The dead man, for the record, is their neighbour Gupta, played by Ravi Kishan. How he ended up in the kitchen is part of the fun. What matters more is what happens after — the series of escalating lies, misunderstandings, and increasingly desperate improvisation that forces the three women to confront not just the body, but each other.

Madhuri Dixit is magnetic here. Rekha is nothing like her usual roles — no grace, no choreography, no romantic softness. She's an outspoken, slightly reckless single mother who wears sleeveless blouses in a town that considers them a moral failing. The character is chaotic and unapologetic, and Dixit plays her with the kind of freedom that suggests she's been waiting a long time for material this sharp. Audiences have noticed. Social media has been full of people who went in expecting something predictable and came out genuinely impressed.

But the scene-stealer is Triptii Dimri. She plays Jaya — the older daughter trapped in a dead-end marriage — with a quiet, simmering frustration that gradually gives way to something fiercer. She starts the film timid. She doesn't end it that way. Decider called her performance the one worth watching even over Dixit's, and they're not wrong. The dynamic between the two is the film's real engine — competitive, protective, unresolved, and entirely believable.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZMiBJYChOt/

And then there's Dharna Durgaa as Sushma, the younger daughter and aspiring influencer, whose comic timing has become one of the most talked-about elements of the film. She brings a loose, improvisational energy that keeps the darker moments from becoming too heavy.

Paresh Rawal makes an appearance too — because apparently this cast wasn't stacked enough.

The comparisons to Darlings are inevitable and fair. Both films use crime as a vehicle for social commentary about the constraints placed on Indian women. But where Darlings leaned toward drama, Maa Behen leans toward absurdity. The satire is baked into the structure: the neighbours are grotesque caricatures of respectability, and the film's sharpest joke is that three women covering up a crime are still less threatening to the moral order than a single mother who doesn't apologise for how she lives.

The reviews from audiences have been overwhelmingly warm. "Sarcastic comedy written so efficiently," reads one reaction. "Social commentary done without being preachy." "Madhuri in a totally different role." "Triptii is here to stay."

For the diaspora, this is a perfect weekend stream. It's on Netflix globally, it runs tight, and it doesn't require any context beyond understanding what it means to be a woman in a small Indian town who refuses to shrink. If you've been waiting for Madhuri Dixit to do something genuinely unexpected, this is it. If you've been tracking Triptii Dimri's ascent from Animal to leading lady, this is the performance that confirms she's arrived.

The body in the kitchen is just the beginning. The real discovery is how good these three women are together.
